text:
noah: Hi all - day 1, followed the WireGuard quickstart but can't reach internal grafana (grafana.internal:3000). DNS resolves to 10.70.3.8 but connection times out. I'm on a coworking space network.
erin: welcome @noah :wave: Coworking NATs can block UDP/ESP which breaks WireGuard. Can you `wg show` and `ip route` and paste the output?
noah: wg show shows latest handshake 2m ago, endpoint shows my-public-ip:51820. ip route default via 192.168.1.1 dev wlan0; 10.70.0.0/16 via 10.0.0.1 dev wg0.
rajesh: if handshake is recent then tunnel is up. Coworking networks sometimes block return-paths for enterprise internal subnets. Quick test: can you SSH to bastion and test curl from there? `ssh -J jump@bastion.redwood.net me@jumpbox` then `curl http://grafana.internal:3000/`
noah: ssh to bastion works, curl from bastion returns 200. So tunnel + DNS ok but coworking provider likely blocking some RFC1918 egress.
erin: short-term: proxy through bastion with SOCKS: `ssh -D 1080 -i ~/.ssh/id_redwood jump@bastion.redwood.net` then `curl -x socks5h://localhost:1080 http://grafana.internal:3000` or set browser to use the SOCKS.
noah: SOCKS works, I can see grafana. For longer term what's the recommended fix?
rajesh: eng-infra options: a) request full-tunnel-onboard tag for your device (temporary full-tunnel VPN) b) use a company-managed mobile hotspot (carrier less likely to rewrite) c) for trusted dev machines we can provision a dedicated short-lived bastion route. File ticket INF-9333 with device name if you want full-tunnel.
noah: filed INF-9333. Also curious if we should add a note in the quickstart about coworking networks.
erin: yes please - devex note to add coworking/tether tips and SOCKS example. Action items: infra to review INF-9333 (rajesh), devex to add coworking note (erin).
noah: thanks everyone, saved my onboarding sprint! :thumbsup:
